description:
Join Apple’s Hardware group and help develop innovative solutions that drive the seamless integration of hardware and software. In this role, you will contribute to building the technology that powers Apple’s products—ensuring they deliver the performance, reliability, and user experience loved by millions around the world. You’ll work at the intersection of hardware and software, solving complex challenges in a highly collaborative and uniquely Apple environment.

Description
In this role, you will develop the tools and flows for managing a single, authoritative description of the hardware/software interface. This includes capturing new architectural requirements from Apple's hardware designs in the common description format and its compiler, ensuring every generated output reflects them correctly, and keeping hardware interface data flowing continuously to software teams for all Apple hardware projects.

This visible and cross-functional role also covers services that make this data accessible across the organization: tracking, searching, browsing, and comparing interface descriptions across projects and releases. The work is full-stack, from low-level C++ development to hosted web services and client user interfaces. It's a close partnership with the designers and software engineers who rely on these tools every day.

Responsibilities
Collaborating with internal hardware design teams and the broader software organization to enable co-development and integration. 
Defining and evolving an IP-XACT-compatible register description format. 
Designing, developing, and maintaining robust, scalable, and intelligent HW/SW interface tools and infrastructure. 
Automating data exchange pipelines to enhance collaboration within Apple and with external vendors.

Minimum qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field
Experience in C++ and Python programming
Experience with git, perforce, or other version control systems

Preferred qualifications
3+ years of relevant industry experience
Knowledge of hardware development fundamentals and chip design concepts
Experience with IP-XACT, SystemRDL, or other hardware register description standards 
Comfortable developing in macOS and Linux environments 
Experience with CI/CD pipelines and automated build systems (GitLab CI, TeamCity, etc.)
Proven ability to work collaboratively across hardware and software teams 
Strong communication skills and ability to articulate technical and architectural concepts 
Understanding of RTL development and design verification methodologies
